Paper: The Impact of the Feed Rate and the Binder Concentration on the Morphology of Spray-Dried Alumina–Polymer Nanocomposites
File: mitra.pdf
Section: summary
Keywords: spray-drying, optimization, process–product relationship, polymer composite, particle technology, image processing, parametric stochastic modeling
Topics: Spray-drying of alumina–polymer nanocomposites, Effects of feed rate and binder concentration on granule morphology, Granule porosity and nano-pore volume/size characterization, Inline and offline particle imaging for morphology analysis, Process–structure relationships and model-based process control
Content: The paper studies spray-drying of nano-alumina with PVP-30 to form alumina–polymer granules and quantifies how feed rate and binder concentration influence granule size, morphology, and porosity. Droplet size/velocity (HiWatch), inline granule imaging (SOPAT), SEM, and mercury intrusion porosimetry are combined to link atomization and process settings to product structure. Higher feed rate increases droplet size/velocity and yields larger, more porous granules, while higher binder concentration makes granules more compact and reduces nano-pore volume, providing a basis for process optimization and model-based control.
title: The Impact of the Feed Rate and the Binder Concentration on the Morphology of Spray-Dried Alumina–Polymer Nanocomposites

text:
Paper: Statistical Analysis and Modeling of the 3D Morphology and Texture of Lunar Regolith Simulants
File: regolith.pdf
Section: summary
Keywords: 3D image data, X-ray micro-CT, regolith simulant, particle descriptor, parametric stochastic model
Topics: 3D morphology and texture characterization of lunar regolith simulants, Comparison of simulant particle morphology to actual lunar regolith, Multivariate distributions of particle size and shape descriptors, Parametric modeling of multivariate non-Gaussian descriptor vectors, Digital twin / stochastic 3D modeling for virtual materials testing and simulations
Content: The paper uses 3D X-ray micro-CT data and multivariate statistical/parametric modeling to quantify size and shape descriptor distributions for lunar regolith particles and seven mare/highlands simulants, finding large morphological differences among simulants and versus lunar regolith and motivating improved simulants or statistically representative digital models for simulation-based studies of morphology-driven mechanical behavior relevant to ISRU. (regolith.pdf p.1, p.2)
title: Statistical Analysis and Modeling of the 3D Morphology and Texture of Lunar Regolith Simulants
